# waroom_postmortem_template (Resource)

Manages a Waroom postmortem template. Postmortem templates provide the initial content of a postmortem.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Write the Markdown content inline with a heredoc.
resource "waroom_postmortem_template" "inline" {
  title = "Standard postmortem"
  blob  = <<-EOT
    # Postmortem

    ## Summary

    ## Impact

    ## Timeline

    ## Root cause

    ## Action items
  EOT
}

# Or read it from a Markdown file placed next to this configuration.
resource "waroom_postmortem_template" "from_file" {
  title = "Security incident postmortem"
  blob  = file("${path.module}/postmortem.md")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `blob` (String) The content of the postmortem template, in Markdown.

### Optional

- `title` (String) The title of the postmortem template.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) The time the postmortem template was created, in RFC 3339 format.
- `id` (String) Postmortem template ID. This is an alias for `uuid`.
- `updated_at` (String) The time the postmortem template was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.
- `uuid` (String) The unique identifier (UUID) of the postmortem template. This is automatically generated by Waroom.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Postmortem templates can be imported by specifying the template UUID
import {
  to = waroom_postmortem_template.inline
  id = "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Postmortem templates can be imported by specifying the template UUID
terraform import waroom_postmortem_template.inline 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
```
